body:
This can be useful if you want to traverse the entire resource file system and extract all translatable strings. You don't even need to implement a parser plugin, you can use a tool script and the static methods.

Unlike `get_previous_parser()`, `get_parser()` generates a warning if no parser is found for the extension, so the obvious way to avoid unwanted warnings is to first check that the parser exists using `get_all_recognized_extensions()`.

But even if we remove the warning, I think it's useful to have access to this information. This method exists in the unexposed singleton `EditorTranslationParser` and similar functionality is available in `ResourceLoader`.

```suggestion
	WARN_PRINT(vformat(R"(No translation parser available for the "%s" extension.)", p_extension));
```
Or
```suggestion
	WARN_PRINT(vformat(R"(No translation parser available for extension "%s".)", p_extension));
```
